memos.headline: S08 and S07 lead on trend and relative strength; S03 and S01 are broken — avoid
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe as of 10/17. S08 is my highest-conviction long: it sits just 2.6% off its 52-week high, trades 4.7% above its 50d and 13.6% above its 200d, with a healthy RSI of 56.5 and 12-week relative strength vs SPY of +13.3% — a textbook uptrend with room to run. S07 has the strongest momentum (+79.6% over 26 weeks, +13.0% over 4 weeks) but RSI at 69.6 and a 16.3% premium to the 50d mean signal an extended move that could snap back; I'd wait for a pullback toward the 50d before adding. On the downside, S03 is firmly in a downtrend — RSI 38.1, 12% off its high, 5.5% below the 50d, and bleeding relative strength at -13.0% over 12 weeks — and S01 is similarly weak at -15.7% drawdown and -6.2% below its 200d. S02 is a bounce-trade only: +28% over 12 weeks but still 43% off its 52-week high and below the 200d mean, so I treat it as a bear-market rally until it reclaims that level.

views.note: Clean uptrend near highs with RSI 56.5 and strong 12w relative strength of +13.3% vs SPY; would reassess on a close below the 50d mean (~241).
Explosive momentum (+79.6% 26w) but RSI 69.6 and 16.3% above 50d mean warn of near-term pullback risk; a dip toward ~454 (50d area) would be a better entry.

Strong 12w bounce (+28%) but still 43% off 52w high and below 200d mean — treat as bear-market rally until price sustains above ~393 (200d area).
Losing relative strength (-5.6% 4w vs SPY), RSI 40.3 trending lower, and -5.5% over 4 weeks; would reconsider on a close back above 310 (50d area).

Treading water near 50d mean with RSI 49.1 and -7.9% drawdown; no trend signal — would get interested on a break above 120 or avoid below 105.

memos.headline: S10 and S04 Lead on Earnings Power; S09 and S02 Flash Cash-Flow Compression Warnings
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between durable growers and names showing earnings erosion. S10 stands out with 55.6% YoY revenue growth, 59.2% YoY net income growth, a 56.5% net margin, and minimal debt at $8.47B — the strongest fundamental profile in the group. S04 also impresses with 18.1% revenue growth, 35.6% net margin, and 23.6% net income growth on a manageable $43.15B debt load. On the other side, S09 posted a -12.4% revenue decline and -23.4% net income drop with an 8.7% margin, while S02 grew revenue 12.9% but saw net income fall 19.2% to a razor-thin 3.1% margin on $79.19B of debt — classic cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for. I would need to see margin stabilization in S09 and S02 before reconsidering, and any deceleration in S10's top-line growth would prompt a downgrade.

views.note: 56.5% net margin, 55.6% YoY revenue growth, minimal leverage at $8.47B debt — best earnings power in the universe.
35.6% net margin with 18.1% revenue growth and 23.6% net income growth on moderate $43.15B debt is durable quality.
29.2% net margin, 13.8% revenue growth, 19.4% net income growth, and low $14.79B debt make this a solid compounder.
13.3% revenue growth and 34.7% net income growth show operating leverage, though 10.8% margin leaves less room for error.
9.6% revenue growth and 24.9% margin are solid but $91.80B debt and decelerating income growth (+9.3%) temper enthusiasm.
15.3% net income growth is encouraging but only 1.7% revenue growth and $30.37B debt on $20.89B revenue limit upside.
33.4% margin is attractive but -10.5% revenue decline, -17.4% income decline, and $419.80B debt are serious headwinds.
Revenue flat at -0.7% YoY with net income down 18.7% and $31.74B debt on $16.57B revenue signals margin erosion.
Revenue down 12.4%, net income down 23.4%, and an 8.7% margin on $33.57B debt is textbook cash-flow compression.
Net income fell 19.2% despite 12.9% revenue growth, leaving a 3.1% margin on $79.19B debt — earnings quality is deteriorating.

memos.headline: Fed in Cautious Easing Mode as Inflation Stays Sticky at 3% YoY and Unemployment Drifts Higher
memos.body: I see the Fed in a slow easing regime: the upper bound is at 4.25%, down 75bp over 12 months, but the pace has slowed to just 25bp over the last three months, consistent with a pause-to-shallow-easing stance. CPI is running at 3.0% YoY—still above target—while unemployment has risen 30bp over both 3- and 12-month horizons to 4.4%, signaling a softening labor market that is not yet alarming. The 10y yield at 4.02% has dropped 45bp over three months, and the 2s10s spread has normalized to +58bp after being inverted a year ago, which is constructive for banks' net interest margins but also reflects growth concerns. I favor duration-sensitive growth and banks over cyclicals and energy in this environment; a CPI print breaking below 2.5% YoY or unemployment jumping above 4.7% would shift my call toward aggressive easing and a more defensive posture.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from falling 10y yields (down 45bp in 3m) and a Fed biased toward further easing.
Banks gain from a positively sloped curve at +58bp 2s10s, a dramatic improvement from near-zero a year ago, supporting NIM expansion.
Staples offer defensive value as unemployment drifts higher, but sticky 3% CPI limits real income gains for consumers.
Cyclicals face headwinds from rising unemployment and a slowing economy; the labor market deterioration argues against pro-cyclical exposure.
Energy is vulnerable if the softening labor market translates into weaker demand; the easing cycle is not yet aggressive enough to reignite growth.
Rate-sensitive sectors benefit as the Fed eases and the 10y yield declines; further cuts would amplify the tailwind.

memos.headline: S06 Earnings Reaction Negative; S07 New Debt Obligation Warrants Monitoring; Limited Sentiment Signal Elsewhere
memos.body: I am reading the 8-K flow across the universe as of 2025-10-17 and find only a handful of actionable sentiment signals. S06 stands out negatively: the Oct 14 earnings 8-K drew a -1.9% price reaction, and the same-day Reg FD filing suggests management felt compelled to get ahead of the narrative—this combination signals tone deterioration that may not yet be fully priced. S07 entered a material definitive agreement creating a direct financial obligation on Sep 3; while not inherently negative, new leverage in this environment is a yellow flag and I see no offsetting positive catalyst. S01 has had a burst of disclosure activity (Reg FD on Oct 14, board changes on Oct 16), which could indicate either proactive governance or internal turbulence—I lean neutral until the narrative clarifies. Across S02, S04, S05, S09, and S10, the filings are routine (Reg FD, director changes, other events) with no measurable price dislocations, so I see no edge from sentiment alone.

views.note: Earnings 8-K triggered a -1.9% sell-off and same-day Reg FD suggests defensive posture; tone is deteriorating.
New material debt obligation filed Sep 3 adds leverage risk but no price reaction data available to gauge market sentiment.
Cluster of Reg FD and board-change filings in mid-October could signal either proactive governance or instability; insufficient to take a directional view.
Aug 27 earnings 8-K produced only a mild -0.8% reaction nearly two months ago; any sentiment signal is stale and likely priced.
Director/officer change on Sep 30 is routine with no accompanying operational disclosure; no sentiment edge.
Back-to-back Reg FD filings in early September with an amendment suggest minor disclosure cleanup, not a narrative shift.

memos.headline: Surging Policy Uncertainty and Collapsing Oil Signal Elevated Geopolitical Risk Across the Universe
memos.body: I am seeing a sharp deterioration in the macro-geopolitical backdrop: the VIX has spiked 55% over the past month to 25.31, while the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index jumped 49% month-over-month to 363.38, suggesting a new policy shock—likely trade or sanctions related—is being priced in. WTI crude at $58.29 is down over 13% in three months, which is unusual if the driver were a supply-side conflict; this points instead to demand destruction from tariff escalation or export-control tightening that is weighing on global growth expectations. HY spreads have widened 25 bps in a month to 3.04%, confirming credit markets are beginning to price stress but not yet at crisis levels. I have low conviction on individual names because the 8-K filings in the universe are generic Reg FD or Other Events disclosures without detail, but the macro regime clearly favors defensiveness and penalizes names with high China/trade exposure or commodity sensitivity.

views.note: Recent Reg FD disclosure suggests proactive investor communication amid uncertainty, but without detail I cannot take a directional view.
Reg FD filing on Oct 14 coincides with the policy-uncertainty spike; management may be front-running bad news, warranting caution but not outright avoidance yet.
Two 8-K Other Events filings in quick succession in early September, combined with the subsequent macro deterioration, suggest elevated operational or regulatory risk.
Back-to-back Reg FD filings in September followed by widening credit spreads keep me on the sideline until the policy picture clarifies.
Oct 6 Reg FD disclosure is too opaque to act on, but the falling oil price environment could be a tailwind if S09 is a net energy consumer.
August 8-K preceded the full policy-uncertainty surge; with VIX up 55% and no clarifying disclosure since, risk-reward is poor.
